title: Meteorite, moon, mars pieces offered at Maastricht auction; Moon slice starts at €25,000

content:
Thursday, 12 November 2026 - 06:30

Auction House Hessink’s is offering 33 pieces of meteorite, a slice of the moon, and a disc of Mars near the Vrijthof in Maastricht. Director and auctioneer Bradley Hessink told L1 it is a unique scale by Dutch standards. The lots range from small fragments to a 102-kilogram specimen that is nearly impossible to lift by hand.

Visitors can already examine and touch the meteorites at the Maastricht premises. The auction begins Saturday.

Hessink expects the large piece to sell for between 500,000 euros and 600,000 euros, while the opening bid on the cheapest meteorite is 150 euros. “Just crazy, unusual things,” he said of the upcoming Space Balls, The Meteorite Auction. Hessink has previously sold works by Banksy and dinosaur skeletons.

Among the objects is a meteorite slab intended as wall decoration and another piece cut into a cube. The cube shows the Widmanstätten pattern, a crystalline structure. Hessink pointed out as proof of authenticity. “You can tell from that this is a real meteorite. You can’t replicate this anywhere on Earth,” he added.

Hessink said the moon piece reached Earth after a meteorite struck the lunar surface, ejecting fragments into space that later fell here. The starting bid for the moon fragment is 25,000 euros.

In a display case, Hessink picked up a framed stone disc from the moon. He referenced a film classic in which a man offers a woman the moon. “Now you have the chance to give your wife a piece of the moon. I personally find that more beautiful than a big stone on a ring,” he told L1.

When asked by the news outlet whether he had given his own wife such a piece. He laughed and replied, “I don’t have the money for that.”

The authenticity has been proven, Hessink said. “We had everything tested, everything is inspected, and everything is certified and sold under a lifelong Hessink’s guarantee.”
